title: Set up pytest infrastructure with initial unit tests
description:
Stand up a real test harness so subsequent refactors can be verified. There is currently no pytest setup — only an ad-hoc script `test_group_notifications.py`.

## What to build
1. `requirements-dev.txt` with: `pytest`, `pytest-cov`, `requests-mock`.
2. `pytest.ini` at repo root with `testpaths = tests`, `pythonpath = .`, and `filterwarnings = ignore::DeprecationWarning`.
3. `tests/__init__.py` (empty) and `tests/unit/__init__.py` (empty).
4. `tests/conftest.py` — provide a `tmp_db_path` fixture that sets `DB_PATH` env var to a tempfile before importing `app.db`, and yields the path. Also provide an `initialized_db` fixture that calls `app.db.init_db()`.
5. `tests/unit/test_url_validation.py` — cover `app.api.endpoints.validate_url` and `normalize_url`: valid domain, valid domain with port, invalid port (out of range, non-numeric), IPv4, localhost, missing scheme (gets https:// prepended), unsupported scheme (ftp://).
6. `tests/unit/test_monitoring_helpers.py` — cover `app.core.monitoring.should_send_down_notification` (fresh notification when last_notified is None, blocked when within interval, allowed when past interval, allowed when last_notified is malformed).

## Files you own
Only create files under `tests/`, and the two top-level config files. Do NOT edit any files in `app/`.

## Acceptance
`pip install -r requirements.txt -r requirements-dev.txt && pytest -x -q` exits 0 and shows at least 10 passing tests.

title: Introduce repositories/DAL layer (new files only, no caller changes)
description:
Every module in the codebase repeats the same `with get_db_connection() as conn: cur = conn.cursor(); cur.execute(...); rows = cur.fetchall()` boilerplate. Introduce a repository layer that centralizes SQL, returns plain dicts/dataclasses, and can be swapped/mocked in tests.

## Scope of THIS task
Only create NEW files under `app/repositories/`. Do NOT edit any existing files (endpoints.py, telegram_bot.py, notifications.py, monitoring.py, etc.) — a follow-up task will migrate callers. Keeping this task file-disjoint prevents merge conflicts with concurrent refactoring work.

## What to build
1. `app/repositories/__init__.py` — re-exports the public repository functions.
2. `app/repositories/endpoints.py` — `list_endpoints()`, `get_endpoint(id)`, `create_endpoint(name, url)`, `update_endpoint(id, name, url)`, `delete_endpoint(id)`, `update_status(id, status, checked_at)`, `mark_down(id, notified_at)`, `mark_up(id, notified_at)`, `update_notified(id, notified_at)`. Raise a small exception hierarchy: `EndpointNotFound`, `EndpointAlreadyExists` (wraps sqlite3.IntegrityError with a nicer message).
3. `app/repositories/subscriptions.py` — `list_subscriptions_for_endpoint(endpoint_id)`, `list_subscriptions_for_chat(chat_id)`, `get_subscription(id)`, `create_subscription(endpoint_id, chat_id, enabled=True)`, `toggle_subscription(id)`, `delete_subscription(id)`, `get_enabled_chat_ids_for_endpoint(endpoint_id)`.
4. `app/repositories/notification_logs.py` — `log_notification(endpoint_url, message, status, timestamp)`, `list_logs(page, per_page, sort_by, order, search, endpoint_filter, status_filter) -> (rows, total_count)`.
5. `app/repositories/settings.py` — `get_all()`, `update(key, value)`. (Do not touch existing `app/db.py:get_settings` — that shim will be replaced later.)
6. `app/repositories/discovery.py` — `find_pending(code)`, `mark_completed(id, chat_id, username, first_name, last_name)`, `create(code, expires_at, created_at)`.

## Conventions
- All functions accept required IDs as arguments and use `app.db.get_db_connection()` internally.
- All read functions return `list[dict]` or `dict | None`; boolean 0/1 columns are cast to Python bool.
- All write functions return the affected id (or None) and call `conn.commit()` inside their own `with` block.
- Use type hints everywhere.
- Do NOT add any tests here — Task 1 owns the test tree.

## Acceptance
All six repository files exist. `python -c "from app.repositories import endpoints, subscriptions, notification_logs, settings, discovery"` exits 0.

title: Fix wrong type annotation in monitoring.py and unify dashboard message formatting
description:
`app/core/monitoring.py` has a bug: `update_notification_time(cur: requests.structures.CaseInsensitiveDict, ...)` — that annotation is nonsense (it is a sqlite3 cursor, not an HTTP header dict). It compiles only because `requests.structures.CaseInsensitiveDict` happens to be importable, but static analysis and readers are misled.

Also, the three notification messages in `check_endpoints_loop` (`[OK] RECOVERED`, `[ALERT] DOWN`, `[WARNING] STILL DOWN`) all hand-format `"...

Dashboard: {config.DASHBOARD_URL}"` inline. Extract a small helper.

## What to change (ONLY this file)
1. Change the parameter annotation on `update_notification_time` from `requests.structures.CaseInsensitiveDict` to `sqlite3.Cursor`. Add `import sqlite3` at the top; drop the unused import chain if no other use of `requests.structures` remains (there is not one).
2. Add a small local helper `_format_alert(kind: str, url: str, status: int) -> str` (module-private, above `check_endpoints_loop`) that returns the message with the dashboard footer. Use it in all three scenarios inside `check_endpoints_loop` so future footer changes happen in one place.
3. Do not change any log strings, control flow, timing, or DB queries. Behavior must be byte-for-byte identical in message TEXT; only the assembly path changes.

## Files you own
`app/core/monitoring.py` — nothing else.

## Acceptance
- `grep -n "CaseInsensitiveDict" app/core/monitoring.py` returns nothing.
- `grep -n "import sqlite3" app/core/monitoring.py` finds the new import.
- `grep -n "_format_alert" app/core/monitoring.py` shows the helper is defined and called at least 3 times.
- `python -c "import app.core.monitoring"` exits 0.

title: Deduplicate Telegram bot subscribe/keyboard logic in telegram_bot.py
description:
`app/core/telegram_bot.py` has significant duplication:

1. `subscribe_to_endpoint_callback` (lines ~325-409) and `subscribe_to_endpoint` (lines ~411-483) implement almost the same subscribe-or-activate logic against two different Update surfaces (callback query vs message). The only real difference is which reply method is called and how the endpoint is fetched.
2. `subscribe_command` (~150-196) and `refresh_endpoints_callback` (~525-566) both build an identical inline keyboard from the endpoint list and post the identical message text.
3. `handler_command` for `/unsubscribe` is currently wired to `list_subscriptions_command` — probably a copy/paste bug but confirm before changing behavior; if intentional, add a short comment noting so.

## What to change (ONLY this file)
1. Extract `_upsert_subscription(cur, endpoint_id: int, chat_id: str) -> tuple[str, str]` returning `(status, endpoint_name)` where status is one of `"already"`, `"reactivated"`, `"created"`. Both `subscribe_to_endpoint_callback` and `subscribe_to_endpoint` should call it and pick the right reply text from a small dict.
2. Extract `_build_endpoint_keyboard(endpoints: list[dict]) -> InlineKeyboardMarkup` and `_ENDPOINT_LIST_TEXT: str` module constants; use them in both `subscribe_command` and `refresh_endpoints_callback`.
3. For the `/unsubscribe` handler wiring: if it is a bug (users expect unsubscribe, not list), rewire to a new small handler that shows only unsubscribe buttons. If preserving old behavior, add a `# NOTE: /unsubscribe intentionally reuses /list to show the unsubscribe buttons inline.` comment on that line.
4. Preserve every user-facing message string exactly. No emoji or wording drift.
5. Do not touch the DB schema, other modules, or add tests (Task 1 owns tests).

## Files you own
`app/core/telegram_bot.py` — nothing else.

## Acceptance
- `grep -c "_upsert_subscription" app/core/telegram_bot.py` returns >= 3 (definition + 2 call sites).
- `grep -c "_build_endpoint_keyboard" app/core/telegram_bot.py` returns >= 3.
- `python -c "import app.core.telegram_bot"` exits 0.
- Net line count of the file drops by at least 80 lines vs before (there is ~180 lines of duplicate code).

title: Extract startup notification logic out of app/__init__.py into app/core/startup.py
description:
`app/__init__.py` is 228 lines because it inlines two big functions: `send_startup_notification` (async orchestrator) and `send_startup_notifications` (sync fan-out with duplicated Telegram loop). This violates the app-factory pattern and duplicates work already in `app/core/notifications.py`.

## What to change
1. Create NEW file `app/core/startup.py` and MOVE both functions there verbatim (preserve every string, log line, comment, and control flow). Fix imports so the moved code still resolves (`from .. import config`, `from ..db import get_db_connection`, `from .notifications import send_group_telegram_notification, send_ntfy_notification`).
2. In `app/__init__.py`:
   - Remove the two function bodies.
   - Add `from .core.startup import send_startup_notification` near the other core imports.
   - Leave `run_background_tasks` calling `send_startup_notification()` unchanged.
   - Remove the now-unused imports (`import requests` inside the deleted body was local; safe to drop). Keep everything else — do NOT touch `create_app`, the Flask setup, CORS, or the `/` route.
3. Do NOT deduplicate the inner Telegram loop against `send_telegram_notification` in this task — a follow-up task will do that once repositories exist. This task is a pure move + import fix so it stays reviewable.

## Files you own

title: Consolidate flask-restx model registration and extract URL validators
description:
Two related quality issues in the API layer:

### 1. Triple-registered models
`add_models_to_api` in `app/models.py` builds and returns a fresh dict of models every time it is called. It is currently called THREE times: once from `app/__init__.py` on the top-level `Api`, once from `app/api/endpoints.py` on its `Namespace`, once from `app/api/settings.py` on its `Namespace`. Each call registers a new model instance — the objects that `endpoints.py:models["endpoint"]` and `__init__.py`s api models refer to are DIFFERENT objects. flask-restx tolerates this but it wastes work and makes the intent unclear.

### 2. URL validation lives in the API layer
`normalize_url` and `validate_url` are defined at the top of `app/api/endpoints.py`. They have no HTTP or Flask dependency and belong in a domain module so tests and future callers (e.g., a CLI) can reuse them.

## What to change
1. Refactor `app/models.py`:
   - Split `add_models_to_api` into two functions:
     - `build_models(api_or_ns)` — the existing body, unchanged (some flask-restx workflows need per-namespace registration for swagger discoverability, so preserve it as-is).
     - Add a module-level cache: `_MODELS: dict | None = None` and `def get_models(api) -> dict:` that lazily calls `build_models(api)` ONCE and returns the cached dict on subsequent calls.
   - Keep `add_models_to_api` as a thin alias for `build_models` for backwards compat with the two namespace files during migration.
2. Update `app/api/endpoints.py`:
   - Move `normalize_url` and `validate_url` (plus the inner `is_valid_ipv4`) to NEW file `app/core/validators.py`.
   - Import them: `from ..core.validators import normalize_url, validate_url`.
   - No behavior change; identical function bodies.
3. Update `app/api/settings.py`: no logic change needed unless it breaks — leave as-is (keeps its `add_models_to_api(ns)` call for now).
4. Create `app/core/validators.py` with the two functions (plus the inner helper made module-private as `_is_valid_ipv4`).

## Files you own
`app/models.py`, `app/api/endpoints.py`, `app/api/settings.py`, and NEW file `app/core/validators.py`. Nothing else. In particular, do NOT touch `app/__init__.py` (Task 5 owns it), `app/core/monitoring.py` (Task 3), `app/core/telegram_bot.py` (Task 4), `app/repositories/*` (Task 2), or `app/core/startup.py` (Task 5).

## Acceptance
- `app/core/validators.py` exists and exports `normalize_url`, `validate_url`.
- `grep -n "def normalize_url" app/api/endpoints.py` returns nothing.
- `grep -n "def validate_url" app/api/endpoints.py` returns nothing.
- `grep -n "def get_models" app/models.py` returns 1 match.
- `python -c "from app.core.validators import normalize_url, validate_url; assert validate_url(\"example.com\"); assert not validate_url(\"not a url with spaces\"); print(normalize_url(\"example.com\"))"` prints `https://example.com` and exits 0.
